subject: Residency & deletion operations Q&A — Helium Health
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@heliumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: privacy@heliumhealth.com
Date: Tue, 05 Nov 2024 14:08:00 +0000
Subject: Quick Q on where requests actually execute (EU requirement)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we liked the latency numbers for eu-west-1. Before we move to legal/procurement, a couple of tight questions from our privacy team:

1) If we enable EU-only processing on Hosted API, can you guarantee that inference requests and any transient logs will never leave the EU (including fallbacks)?
2) Which subprocessors in the chain have access to payloads or decrypted telemetry (e.g., logging/alerting services, backup targets)?
3) What's your deletion flow if we ask to purge all Helium Health data (requests, cache, logs)? How long until physical removal from backups?

We need answers we can attach to the DPA. Short bullets are perfect.

Tom
Head of Privacy Ops
Helium Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Nov 2024 15:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests actually execute (EU requirement)

Tom — thanks for the clear list. Short answers here; attaching a one-page residency diagram and a DPA draft for legal. Full subprocessor roster is in the attachment.

1) EU-only processing: Yes — for accounts provisioned in the EU region we serve inference and associated short-term telemetry from EU compute (primary: AWS eu-west-1, secondary: GCP europe-west3 for dedicated/private where requested). Our hosted control plane is global but we offer a EU-only hosting tier. By default we route to the account's region and pin compute.

2) Subprocessors with potential access to plaintext/transient telemetry: AWS (eu-west-1), Google Cloud (europe-west3) when explicitly used, Fastly (edge routing for API traffic), Datadog (metrics and optional traces), Sentry (error payloads if enabled), and HashiCorp Vault or AWS KMS for key management. We do not send customer request bodies to analytics vendors by default. Full list + contracts in the attached PDF.

3) Deletion flow: immediate logical deletion request accepted via Console/API -> our system soft-deletes objects and invalidates caches immediately -> physical purge windows below. For hosted EU accounts our standard timeline: transient request payloads and KV cache entries: evicted immediately; application-level logs and debug payloads: removed within 30 days; backups and snapshots: purged per backup retention (default max 90 days) unless an enterprise SLA shortens it. We can contractually shorten retention windows for Dedicated/Private with addenda.

Notes on fallbacks: we only fail over across regions in two cases — (a) if the customer has explicitly enabled cross-region fallback in their routing policy, or (b) in a platform-wide emergency where we notify customers and follow the emergency exception in the DPA. For EU-only accounts the default is to not enable cross-region fallback.

I'll loop in Ben for subprocessor legalities and Karthik for deletion SLAs.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-eu-processing-overview.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, privacy@heliumhealth.com
Date: Wed, 06 Nov 2024 09:26:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests actually execute (EU requirement)

Tom — adding a bit of legal/operational color on subprocessors and access controls.

- Subprocessor access: most infra subprocessors (AWS/GCP) have access to compute nodes but we use encryption-in-transit and KMS-backed encryption-at-rest. Only our runtime layer (Redwood process) ever has access to the unencrypted request payloads to perform inference. Logging/monitoring vendors (Datadog, Sentry) receive redacted telemetry by default; error payloads are opt-in and explicitly gated.

- Key management: for EU customers we recommend using customer-managed keys in AWS KMS or a dedicated HSM; this prevents our support engineers from decrypting stored artifacts without an explicit key release process.

- Backup removal: backups are retained according to the schedule in the DPA. For customers who need an expedited purge we offer an expedited deletion addendum for Dedicated/Private deployments: we can drive physical destruction of snapshots within 7–14 days and confirm via signed attestation. For Hosted plans the standard is up to 90 days unless contractually amended.

- Cross-border transfers: by default we do not replicate customer inference payloads outside the account region. We do replicate aggregated operational metrics (non-identifying) for platform health unless the customer opts out on an enterprise plan. Any forced cross-border processing for continuity is subject to escalation and a formal notification process.

If you want, we can provide our standard SCCs plus the tailored DPA changes that reflect the non-replication guarantee.

Thanks,
Ben
Head of Customer Security — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, privacy@heliumhealth.com
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2024 15:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests actually execute (EU requirement)

Tom — following up with SLA/deletion commitments we can put in the contract for Helium Health:

- Residency SLA: For Procured EU-hosted accounts we guarantee that inference compute and transient request logs will be processed only in the EU region (eu-west-1 or customer-specified EU region). We will not enable cross-region failover without written customer authorization.

- Deletion SLA: On receipt of a 'full purge' request we will: (1) apply immediate logical deletion, (2) evict KV/prefix caches within minutes, (3) remove application logs and any debug payloads within 30 calendar days (by default) and (4) remove or rotate backups within up to 90 calendar days for standard hosted. For Dedicated/Private customers we can contract to a 7–14 day final-physical-delete window and provide attestation.

- Audit evidence: we will provide a subprocessor roster, our SOC 2 Type II report, and exportable evidence (redacted) of deletion operations.

Next steps: if this matches your needs we (1) attach the tailored DPA and SCCs, (2) sign the expedited deletion addendum for Dedicated-like guarantees, or (3) if you need on-prem, we can scope a Private deployment.

Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
